title: A request to Vault
summary: A caller logs in, is checked against a policy and receives a secret.

steps.n: The application presents an identity such as a service account token.
Vault returns a token with policies and a time to live.
The application sends the token with a request for a path.
The policy check allows read on that path.
The engine returns the secret with a lease.
Vault records who asked, which path, and the outcome, with values hashed.

title: Failure and recovery: a sealed Vault after reboot
summary: Vault restarts sealed and is brought back with auto-unseal.

steps.n: The Vault node reboots after a kernel patch.
Vault finds its encrypted data but cannot read it.
Applications receive errors because Vault is sealed.
Only one of five key holders is reachable, so the threshold is not met.
The team configures a cloud KMS key to unwrap the root key at start.
At the next restart Vault asks the KMS to unwrap the root key.
Vault unseals in seconds without a person.
Requests succeed again and the team records a restart test in the runbook.

title: Kubernetes login
summary: A pod proves its identity and receives a short-lived Vault token.

steps.n: The pod sends its service account token to the Kubernetes auth method.
Vault asks the Kubernetes API to confirm the token is genuine.
Vault checks the service account name and namespace against the role.
The matching role gives the policies that the token will carry.
Vault returns a token with a one hour TTL.
Before expiry the pod renews the token or logs in again.

title: How a policy decides
summary: Vault compares a request path with the policies on the token.

steps.n: The client sends a read of secret/data/billing/db with its token.
Policy A allows read under secret/data/billing/*.
Policy B grants nothing on that path.
The capabilities from all policies are merged and a deny would win.
The merged result includes read, so Vault returns the secret.
A read of secret/data/payments/db matches no rule and is denied.

title: Two writers and check-and-set
summary: Check-and-set stops a second writer from overwriting a newer version.

steps.n: Engineer A reads the secret and sees version 1.
Engineer B also reads version 1.
Engineer A writes a new value naming version 1 as the base.
The engine accepts the write and creates version 2.
Engineer B writes naming version 1, which is no longer current.
The engine rejects it, so B reads version 2 and merges the change.

title: A dynamic database credential
summary: Vault creates a user, hands it out with a lease, and drops it at expiry.

steps.n: The application reads database/creds/orders-ro.
Vault runs the creation SQL with its admin account.
It records a one hour lease for the new user.
The application receives a unique login that only it holds.
After an hour the lease ends without a renewal.
Vault runs the revocation SQL and the credential stops working.

title: Issuing a 24 hour certificate
summary: A service requests a certificate from an intermediate CA.

steps.n: The service asks the PKI role for a certificate for api.svc.example.internal.
Vault checks the domain and the maximum TTL allowed by the role.
The intermediate CA signs a certificate valid for 24 hours.
The service receives the private key, certificate and chain.
A client verifies the chain up to the root it trusts.
After about 16 hours the service requests a fresh certificate.

title: Encrypting a card number
summary: The application never holds the key, only ciphertext.

steps.n: The application sends a base64 encoded card number to transit/encrypt/orders.
Vault encrypts it with the current version of the orders key.
Vault returns vault:v3:... and the application stores it.
The database holds only ciphertext.
A backup is copied by mistake and the auditor reviews it.
The auditor finds only ciphertext, and the key is not in the backup.

title: Failure and recovery: a pod that cannot mount its secret
summary: A role binding mismatch keeps the init container from finishing.

steps.n: A pod with injector annotations is created in the shop namespace.
The injector adds an init container and a sidecar for Vault Agent.
The agent sends the pod's service account token to Vault.
Vault compares the service account to the role binding.
The role names the service account order but the pod uses orders.
The init container never finishes so the pod does not start.
The operator reads the role and sees the mismatch.
The role is corrected to the right service account and the pod starts.

title: Leader failure in a Raft cluster
summary: A standby takes over when the active node fails.

steps.n: The client sends a write through the load balancer.
The balancer sends it to the node that reports itself active.
The active node replicates the write to standbys.
The active node crashes after a hardware fault.
The standbys hold an election and one becomes the leader.
The load balancer sees the new active node and routes there.

title: Failure and recovery: the audit disk fills
summary: Vault stops answering because it cannot write its audit log.

steps.n: Clients send requests and Vault answers them.
Each request is logged to the audit device.
Logs are never rotated and the disk reaches 100 percent.
Vault cannot write to its only audit device.
Vault refuses all requests rather than operate without a record.
The operator frees space and rotates the logs.
A second audit device and a disk alert are added.
Vault answers requests again and logs to two devices.

title: Responding to a leaked token
summary: Contain, investigate and rotate after a token is exposed.

steps.n: A scanner reports a token in a public repository.
The responder looks up the accessor and revokes the token.
Dynamic credentials issued to it are revoked by prefix.
The log shows which paths the token read and from where.
Each static secret the token read is replaced at its source.
The new values are written to Vault and consumers restarted.
